scenes.tts: Plants often respire roughly half of the energy they fix. So where does the rest go? Take one square metre for one year, in a made-up budget. The producers fix twelve thousand kilojoules. That is gross primary production. The producers respire six thousand of it, and it leaves as heat. What is left is net primary production, six thousand.

scenes.tts: Now herbivores eat. They ingest eighteen hundred kilojoules, which is thirty percent of the net primary production. The other forty two hundred is never grazed. It dies and enters detritus. Detritus is dead matter that feeds bacteria, fungi and animals that eat detritus.
scenes.caption: Now herbivores eat. They ingest 1,800 kilojoules, which is 30% of the net primary production. The other 4,200 is never grazed. It dies and enters detritus. Detritus is dead matter that feeds bacteria, fungi and animals that eat detritus.
scenes.visual: Producer box moves left; herbivore box appears with an arrow carrying 1,800; the remaining 4,200 flows down into a detritus box.
scenes.narration: Now herbivores eat. They ingest 1,800 kilojoules, which is 30% of the net primary production. The other 4,200 is never grazed. It dies and enters detritus. Detritus is dead matter that feeds bacteria, fungi and animals that eat detritus.

scenes.tts: Follow the herbivores. They ingest eighteen hundred. They egest one thousand eighty as feces. The other seven hundred twenty is assimilated. The herbivores respire three hundred sixty as heat. The last three hundred sixty is production, new tissue and offspring. The three efficiencies are thirty, forty and fifty percent. Multiplied, they give a transfer efficiency of six percent.
scenes.caption: Follow the herbivores. They ingest 1,800. They egest 1,080 as feces. The other 720 is assimilated. The herbivores respire 360 as heat. The last 360 is production, new tissue and offspring. The three efficiencies are 30, 40 and 50%. Multiplied, they give a transfer efficiency of 6%.
scenes.visual: The 1,800 slice of the NPP bar becomes a bar that splits into egested, respired and production segments; three efficiencies multiply to 6%.
scenes.narration: Follow the herbivores. They ingest 1,800. They egest 1,080 as feces. The other 720 is assimilated. The herbivores respire 360 as heat. The last 360 is production, new tissue and offspring. The three efficiencies are 30, 40 and 50%. Multiplied, they give a transfer efficiency of 6%.

scenes.tts: Predators keep the same books. Of the herbivores' three hundred sixty of production, they ingest two hundred. The other one hundred sixty goes to detritus. The predators egest one hundred and respire sixty. Their production is forty. That is a transfer efficiency of eleven percent, against six for the first link. So no single number describes both links.
scenes.caption: Predators keep the same books. Of the herbivores' 360 of production, they ingest 200. The other 160 goes to detritus. The predators egest 100 and respire 60. Their production is 40. That is a transfer efficiency of 11%, against 6% for the first link. So no single number describes both links.

scenes.tts: Now the detritus. Ungrazed plants, feces and uneaten animal production all arrive there. Together they come to five thousand five hundred forty. The decomposers respire three thousand two hundred forty of it as heat. That leaves twenty three hundred. Notice that the decomposers respired more than every animal combined. In this budget, most net primary production never passed through an animal.

scenes.tts: Now add it up. Respiration totals nine thousand six hundred sixty. Twelve thousand fixed, minus that, leaves net ecosystem production of twenty three hundred forty. That is the detritus plus the predators' production. The ledger closes. Suppose each step passes on ten percent. Then level four gets a tenth of one percent of net primary production. But ten percent is a rough benchmark from aquatic models, not a law. Keep rates in matching units, and keep the detritus in the budget.
